- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.1) and prices are falling, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not drop below 1–2% below recent low.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate in high-sentiment periods; adjust upward by 1–3% if sentiment >0.3 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–0.2) and prices are erratic, model often fails to capture short-term reversals; use 2-day moving average of true values as anchor for next forecast.
